context_refs: Current Gepetto local installation and data
Existing Gmail/Google Calendar bridge must remain functional
Existing project inventory must be migrated/reused, not discarded
prompt:
You are implementing Gepetto V2 on the user's existing local Gepetto application. Work directly on the actual local codebase and data. First audit architecture, data locations, current modules, bridges, routing, UI, and startup path. Make a safety backup or reversible git checkpoint before invasive edits. Preserve all existing user data and working integrations. Do not buy or introduce paid services. Prefer the current stack and dependencies; add only lightweight free/open-source dependencies when genuinely useful.

PRODUCT DIRECTION
Gepetto V2 is an AI-native Personal OS, not a conventional project manager. Its purpose is to make the user's domains, projects, notes, habits/capabilities, resources, calendar items, emails, decisions, ideas and archives feel interconnected and easy to navigate. The current problem is fragmentation: separate project lists, fake Milanote/corkboard pages, calendar, chat and modules that do not share one coherent model. V2 must connect them.

CORE INFORMATION MODEL
Create or adapt a unified entity/relationship model underneath the existing app. Support at minimum these entity types: DOMAIN, PROJECT, NOTE, IDEA, DECISION, TASK/ACTION, HABIT_OR_CAPABILITY, RESOURCE, DOCUMENT_OR_MEDIA, CALENDAR_EVENT_REF, EMAIL_REF, SALE_OR_ORDER when relevant, ARCHIVE_SOURCE. Entities can belong to one or several domains/projects and have typed links. Do not force everything to be a PROJECT. Example: the existing 'Régie' in the Video area is a recurring capability/habit/workspace, not a project, and must be represented accordingly. Existing modules/capabilities should remain usable but become linked entities inside domains rather than disconnected top-level islands.

MIGRATION
Inventory all existing Gepetto projects and domain/module data. Build a non-destructive migration/adaptation layer so current projects appear in the new model. Preserve legacy identifiers/source references. If categorisation is ambiguous, retain the item and mark it for review rather than deleting or guessing destructively. Existing completed projects should remain accessible as completed/archived. Existing Gmail/Google Calendar bridge logic must remain available.

MAIN NAVIGATION / BUBBLE UX
Replace the fake corkboard/Milanote-style project navigation as the primary UX with an elegant bubble system. At the global level, show domains. Opening a domain such as Vidéo shows project/capability bubbles. Within a domain, each project is a bubble. Bubble proximity to the visual centre represents current importance/attention; bubble size can reinforce importance but must remain readable. Status/health may use restrained pastel semantic colour. Avoid gamified/mobile-game styling.

The target art direction is clean, modern, organic, airy and pastel. Off-white/light neutral background, subtle texture, soft pastel blue/green/pink/beige, excellent typography, elegant serif for major headings paired with highly readable sans-serif UI text. No Mac red/yellow/green window dots. No profile avatar in the header. Keep a simple Gepetto V2 title, search, and a small settings control. Side navigation/panels should be retractable or represented as slim edge handles so the user can get a nearly pure bubble canvas.

MICRO-ANIMATIONS
Implement restrained, tasteful interaction. On pointer hover over a bubble: smoothly scale by roughly 4-7%, slightly strengthen shadow/halo and raise z-index; return smoothly on pointer leave. Duration around 160-240ms, easing such as cubic-bezier(0.2,0.8,0.2,1). Include extremely subtle slow levitation/drift where it does not hurt accessibility/performance, preferably transform-only. Selected bubble may gently focus while nearby bubbles recede a little. Respect prefers-reduced-motion and disable nonessential motion when requested by OS. Do not make it kitsch, bouncy or neon.

PROJECT OPEN STATE
Clicking a project bubble should transition into a full, readable project workspace. The clicked bubble should feel conceptually like it expands into the page, but implementation can use routing/state + transition rather than complex physics. Show:
- breadcrumb Domain > Project
- project title + concise purpose/subtitle
- status and counters (notes, key ideas, next actions)
- 'Rapport de Gepetto': an automatically generated/current summary area describing where the project stands, what is going well, weak points/blockers, next leverage points, stale areas and recent changes
- Notes area with concise titles/excerpts and easy create/edit/open interactions
- Idées importantes area, allowing promotion/demotion/tagging/linking of ideas
- Prochaines actions checklist
- Documents & médias area supporting images, videos and files/links already supported by the stack
- related entities/projects as small linked bubbles
- activity/history/source provenance when available
Do not overwhelm with raw text dumps. Long imported reports should be kept as source/archive and decomposed into useful structured entities/summaries while preserving provenance.

DOMAIN OPEN STATE
When opening a domain, display its bubbles and a lightweight contextual summary: number of projects, notes, active/urgent items, and a concise Gepetto status sentence. Allow panels to retract. Search should find projects, notes and ideas.

TODAY / CALENDAR
Keep Google Calendar relevant, but integrate it contextually rather than as a disconnected page. Calendar events may be linked to projects/actions. A compact 'Aujourd'hui' view/strip is desirable if it can reuse the existing integration without destabilising it. Do not break the existing Gmail bridge or Calendar workflow.

AI / REPORT LOGIC
If there is already an AI/chat layer, reuse it. Gepetto's assistant should operate contextually: when inside a domain/project, it should know that context and be able to create/link notes, ideas and actions. The project report must have a deterministic fallback based on project metadata/activity when AI is unavailable, so the UI never becomes empty or broken. Do not require a new paid API.

PERFORMANCE / TECHNICAL QUALITY
Do not open unnecessary external browser tabs for internal sections. Internal domain/project transitions must be SPA/local-app navigation and feel fast. Bubble animation should use transform/opacity where possible. Avoid expensive continuous re-layout. Preserve keyboard accessibility, visible focus states, labels/tooltips, responsive layout and reduced-motion support.

IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGY
1) Audit and document current architecture + data. 2) Checkpoint/backup. 3) Introduce unified model/adapters. 4) Implement bubble domain view behind a safe V2 route/feature flag if necessary. 5) Implement project workspace. 6) Connect existing projects and capability modules. 7) Integrate related notes/ideas/actions/media and Calendar references where already possible. 8) Add micro-animations + retractable panels. 9) Migrate existing navigation to V2 once stable, while leaving an escape path to legacy temporarily if prudent. 10) Run available tests/build/lint and launch smoke tests.

DELIVERABLE
Make actual code changes, not only a plan. Produce a working V2 prototype integrated into Gepetto with real existing data where possible. At completion, return a precise GPTO_CODEX_RESULT/1 with files changed, tests run/results, what was migrated, what remains legacy, any blockers, and exact steps for the user to launch/test the V2. If the codebase location or architecture differs from assumptions, adapt intelligently rather than stopping. If something risky cannot be safely automated, implement the safest surrounding pieces and report the one precise manual step needed.
